The shape of the hadronic form factor f+(q2) in the decay D0 --> K- e+ nue has been measured in a model independent analysis and compared with theoretical calculations. We use 75 fb(-1) of data recorded by the BABAR detector at the PEPII electron-positron collider. The corresponding decay branching fraction, relative to the decay D0 --> K- pi+, has also been measured to be RD = BR(D0 --> K- e+ nue)/BR(D0 --> K- pi+) = 0.927 +/- 0.007 +/- 0.012. From these results, and using the present world average value for BR(D0 --> K- pi+), the normalization of the form factor at q2=0 is determined to be f+(0)=0.727 +/- 0.007 +/- 0.005 +/- 0.007 where the uncertainties are statistical, systematic, and from external inputs, respectively.

outputs.L1:
The shape of the hadronic form factor \(f_+(q^2)\) in the decay \(D^0 \to K^- e^+ \nu_e\) has been measured through a model-independent analysis and compared with theoretical calculations. The study uses \(75\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}\) of data recorded by the BABAR detector at the PEP-II electron–positron collider. The corresponding decay branching fraction, measured relative to the decay \(D^0 \to K^- \pi^+\), is

\[
R_D = \frac{\mathrm{BR}(D^0 \to K^- e^+ \nu_e)}{\mathrm{BR}(D^0 \to K^- \pi^+)}
= 0.927 \pm 0.007 \pm 0.012.
\]

Using these results together with the current world-average value of \(\mathrm{BR}(D^0 \to K^- \pi^+)\), the normalization of the form factor at \(q^2 = 0\) is determined to be

\[
f_+(0) = 0.727 \pm 0.007 \pm 0.005 \pm 0.007,
\]

where the uncertainties are statistical, systematic, and due to external inputs, respectively.

The branching fraction for this decay, measured relative to D⁰ → K⁻ π⁺, is found to be:

R_D = BR(D⁰ → K⁻ e⁺ νₑ) / BR(D⁰ → K⁻ π⁺) = 0.927 ± 0.007 ± 0.012.

Combining this measurement with the current world-average value of BR(D⁰ → K⁻ π⁺), the form-factor normalization at q² = 0 is obtained as:

f₊(0) = 0.727 ± 0.007 ± 0.005 ± 0.007,

The shape of the hadronic form factor \(f_+(q^2)\) in the semileptonic decay \(D^0 \to K^- e^+ \nu_e\) was measured using a model-independent analysis. This form factor describes the strong-interaction dynamics of the \(D^0 \to K^-\) transition and is an essential input for determining charm-sector weak interaction parameters.

The analysis was performed using a data sample corresponding to an integrated luminosity of \(75\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}\), recorded with the BABAR detector at the PEP-II electron-positron collider. The large data set allowed a detailed study of the \(q^2\) dependence of the decay rate, where \(q^2\) is the squared four-momentum transferred to the lepton-neutrino system.

The relative branching fraction of the semileptonic decay with respect to the hadronic normalization mode \(D^0 \to K^- \pi^+\) was measured to be

\[
R_D =
\frac{\mathrm{BR}(D^0 \to K^- e^+ \nu_e)}
{\mathrm{BR}(D^0 \to K^- \pi^+)}
=
0.927 \pm 0.007 \pm 0.012,
\]

where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second is systematic.

Using the world-average value of \(\mathrm{BR}(D^0 \to K^- \pi^+)\), the normalization of the form factor at zero momentum transfer was determined to be

\[
f_+(0) = 0.727 \pm 0.007 \pm 0.005 \pm 0.007.
\]

The uncertainties correspond respectively to the statistical uncertainty, the experimental systematic uncertainty, and the uncertainty associated with the external input branching fraction. This result provides an important test of theoretical calculations of charm semileptonic decays and contributes to improved determinations of the relevant Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix elements.

A measurement of the hadronic form factor \(f_{+}(q^{2})\) in the semileptonic decay \(D^{0} \to K^{-} e^{+} \nu_{e}\) was performed using a model-independent analysis of a data sample corresponding to \(75\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}\) collected with the BABAR detector. In this decay, the variable \(q^{2}\) represents the squared four-momentum transferred to the lepton-neutrino system, and the form factor \(f_{+}(q^{2})\) describes the strong-interaction effects governing the transition from the charm quark to the strange quark inside the meson. Because these nonperturbative effects cannot be calculated directly from first principles with simple analytic methods, precise experimental measurements are essential for testing theoretical approaches such as lattice QCD and other form-factor parameterizations.

The analysis determined the shape of \(f_{+}(q^{2})\) without relying on a specific model for its \(q^{2}\) dependence, allowing a direct comparison with theoretical predictions. The measured decay distribution was used to extract the ratio

\[
R_{D} = 0.927 \pm 0.007 \pm 0.012,
\]

where the uncertainties are statistical and systematic, respectively. In addition, the normalization of the form factor at zero momentum transfer was found to be

\[
f_{+}(0) = 0.727 \pm 0.007 \pm 0.005 \pm 0.007.
\]

The quoted uncertainties reflect the statistical contribution, the experimental systematic uncertainty, and an additional uncertainty associated with external inputs.

These results provide a precise determination of the normalization and behavior of the \(D^{0} \to K^{-} e^{+} \nu_{e}\) form factor. Such measurements are important because semileptonic charm decays offer a clean environment for studying the interplay between weak and strong interactions. The value of \(f_{+}(0)\), in particular, serves as a key benchmark for theoretical calculations and helps validate methods used to describe hadronic effects in heavy-flavor physics. By comparing the BABAR measurement with theoretical predictions, the study contributes to improved tests of semileptonic charm-decay theory and supports the broader effort to refine determinations of quark-mixing parameters in the Standard Model.
outputs.L5:
The BABAR experiment was a major particle physics experiment designed to study the differences between matter and antimatter. It operated at the PEP-II electron-positron collider at the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory in California.

PEP-II was an asymmetric-energy collider, meaning it collided electrons and positrons at different energies. These collisions produced large numbers of B mesons, which were then observed by the BABAR detector. By studying how these particles decayed, scientists were able to investigate CP violation, a phenomenon that helps explain why the universe contains more matter than antimatter.

The BABAR collaboration included researchers from many institutions around the world. Its results made important contributions to the Standard Model of particle physics, especially in the study of B meson decays, rare processes, and the behavior of fundamental particles.

Although PEP-II and the BABAR detector are no longer taking data, the experiment’s scientific legacy remains significant. The data collected by BABAR continues to be analyzed, helping physicists test theories and search for signs of new physics beyond the Standard Model.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a particle physics paper reporting a BABAR measurement of the hadronic form factor in \(D^0 \to K^- e^+ \nu_e\) using 75 fb\(^{-1}\), including the relative branching fraction and extracted \(f_+(0)\).
counterfactuals.output:
Abstract: We report a measurement of the hadronic form factor in the semileptonic decay \(D^0 \to K^- e^+ \nu_e\) using a data sample corresponding to an integrated luminosity of \(75\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}\) collected with the BABAR detector at the PEP-II \(e^+e^-\) storage rings. The decay is reconstructed using \(D^{*+}\to D^0\pi^+\) tags, and the semileptonic branching fraction is measured relative to the normalization mode \(D^0\to K^-\pi^+\). We find
\[
\frac{\mathcal{B}(D^0\to K^- e^+\nu_e)}
{\mathcal{B}(D^0\to K^-\pi^+)}
=
0.9269 \pm 0.0072 \pm 0.0119,
\]
where the uncertainties are statistical and systematic, respectively. The dependence of the decay rate on the squared momentum transfer \(q^2\) is used to determine the shape of the vector form factor \(f_+(q^2)\). From the measured decay rate and using external inputs for \(\mathcal{B}(D^0\to K^-\pi^+)\), the \(D^0\) lifetime, and \(|V_{cs}|\), we extract
\[
f_+(0)=0.727 \pm 0.007 \pm 0.005 \pm 0.007,
\]
where the uncertainties are statistical, systematic, and due to external inputs, respectively. The measured form-factor shape is consistent with expectations from semileptonic charm-decay phenomenology and provides a precise test of theoretical calculations of heavy-to-light hadronic matrix elements.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

\[
D^0 \to K^- e^+ \nu_e
\]

using \(D^{*+}\to D^0\pi^+\) tagged events and normalizing to the hadronic mode \(D^0\to K^-\pi^+\). Rather than assuming a specific pole model for the \(q^2\) dependence, BABAR measured the partial decay rates in bins of \(q^2\), thereby extracting the shape of \(f_+(q^2)\) directly.

The measured ratio of branching fractions was

\[
R_D \equiv 
\frac{\mathcal B(D^0\to K^- e^+\nu_e)}
{\mathcal B(D^0\to K^-\pi^+)}
=
0.9269 \pm 0.0072_{\rm stat} \pm 0.0119_{\rm syst}.
\]

Using the known \(D^0\to K^-\pi^+\) branching fraction and \(|V_{cs}|\), BABAR obtained

\[
f_+(0) = 0.727
\pm 0.007_{\rm stat}
\pm 0.005_{\rm syst}
\pm 0.007_{\rm ext},
\]

where the last uncertainty comes from external inputs such as \(|V_{cs}|\) and the normalization branching fraction.

They found that the measured \(q^2\) dependence is well described by more flexible parameterizations such as the modified pole or series expansion, while a simple pole fit gives an effective pole mass below the physical \(D_s^*\) mass, indicating that a naive single-pole model is not adequate for the form-factor shape.

\[
\frac{{\cal B}(D^0\to K^- e^+\nu_e)}
     {{\cal B}(D^0\to K^-\pi^+)}
= 0.9269 \pm 0.0072 \,(\mathrm{stat}) \pm 0.0119 \,(\mathrm{syst}) .

Using the known \(D^0\to K^-\pi^+\) branching fraction, this corresponds to

\[

= (3.52 \pm 0.03 \,(\mathrm{stat}) \pm 0.05 \,(\mathrm{syst}) \pm 0.07 \,(\mathrm{norm}))\% .
\]

From the measured \(q^2\) dependence of the decay rate, the vector form-factor normalization is determined to be

\[
f_+^K(0) = 0.727 \pm 0.007 \,(\mathrm{stat}) \pm 0.005 \,(\mathrm{syst}) \pm 0.007 \,(\mathrm{ext}) ,

consistent with contemporary lattice-QCD expectations and providing a precision test of charm semileptonic form-factor calculations.

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a journal-style summary of a model-independent analysis of the hadronic form factor \(f_+(q^2)\) in \(D^0 \to K^- e^+ \nu_e\), including comparison to theory, dataset size, BABAR detector, and uncertainties.
counterfactuals.output:
### Journal-style summary

A model-independent study of the hadronic vector form factor \(f_+(q^2)\) in the semileptonic decay  
\[
D^0 \to K^- e^+ \nu_e
\]
has been performed using data collected with the **BABAR detector** at the PEP-II \(e^+e^-\) collider. The analysis uses an integrated luminosity of approximately **347 fb\(^{-1}\)** recorded near the \(\Upsilon(4S)\) resonance, corresponding to a large sample of charm events produced in continuum \(e^+e^- \to c\bar c\) processes.

The decay is reconstructed through the tagged chain  
\[
D^{*+}\to D^0\pi^+,\qquad D^0\to K^- e^+\nu_e,
\]
where the slow pion from the \(D^{*+}\) decay provides a clean flavor tag and suppresses combinatorial background. The neutrino four-momentum is inferred from event missing momentum, and kinematic constraints are used to improve the resolution in the momentum-transfer variable \(q^2\).

The differential decay rate is proportional to  
\[
\frac{d\Gamma}{dq^2} \propto |V_{cs}|^2\, |f_+(q^2)|^2\, p_K^3 ,
\]
where \(p_K\) is the kaon momentum in the \(D^0\) rest frame. Rather than assuming a specific pole-dominance model, the form-factor shape is described using a **model-independent series expansion**, often expressed in terms of the conformal variable \(z\). This approach exploits analyticity and unitarity constraints and reduces sensitivity to model assumptions in the extrapolation over the physical \(q^2\) range.

The measured \(q^2\) spectrum is unfolded for detector resolution and efficiency, and the normalized form-factor shape \(f_+(q^2)/f_+(0)\) is extracted. The result is consistent with modern theoretical expectations, including unquenched lattice-QCD calculations and light-cone sum-rule predictions in their respective regions of validity. Simple pole parameterizations are found to give an effective pole mass below the physical \(D_s^{*}\) pole, illustrating the limitations of overly restrictive phenomenological models. Modified pole and series-expansion descriptions provide significantly improved agreement with the data.

Using external input for \(|V_{cs}|\), or alternatively comparing with lattice-QCD calculations of \(f_+(0)\), the analysis obtains a normalization consistent with Standard Model expectations. A representative result is
\[
f_+(0)|V_{cs}| \simeq 0.72\text{--}0.73,
\]
which, with \(|V_{cs}|\) taken from CKM unitarity, corresponds to
\[
f_+(0) \simeq 0.74\text{--}0.75,
\]
in good agreement with lattice-QCD predictions.

The dominant uncertainties arise from signal and background modeling, reconstruction efficiencies, particle identification, neutrino reconstruction, and the unfolding of the \(q^2\) spectrum. Statistical uncertainties are small owing to the large BABAR data sample, while systematic uncertainties dominate several aspects of the shape and normalization determination. Correlations among the measured \(q^2\) bins and among the fitted series-expansion coefficients are essential for quantitative comparison with theory.

Overall, the BABAR measurement provides a precise, model-independent determination of the \(D^0\to K^- e^+\nu_e\) form-factor shape. It offers an important test of lattice-QCD calculations in charm semileptonic decays and supports the reliability of theoretical methods used to extract CKM matrix elements from heavy-flavor semileptonic processes.
